newsitem.title: FINLAND: Aamulehti says MTV valued in line.
newsitem.headline: Aamulehti says MTV valued in line.

text.p: The value of commercial television operator MTV Oy in a planned merger with media group Aamulehti is in line with printing and broadcast values in stock markets, Aamulehti CEO Matti Packalen said on Tuesday.

The two said they planned to merge at the turn of next year, with each of Aamulehti's shares -- 9.62 million assuming full conversion of bonds -- giving one share in the new company and each of MTV's 55,000 shares giving 137.5 shares in it.
Aamulehti's current 20.3 percent stake in MTV will be annulled.
Packalen said the ratio was fair and based on a discounted cash-flow analysis which had been compared to a price/earnings multiple analysis, and finally sealed by negotiations.

"The P/E ratio behind the conversion rate was quite in line with other companies," he said, adding that in general, broadcasters' historical P/E ratios 1996 were about 24 and those of printing houses about 16-17.

An analyst told Reuters that shares in MTV, which is unlisted, have recently traded between 10,000 and 14,000 markka each in the grey over-the-counter market -- 9.6 to 13.4 times MTV's 1996 1,043 markka EPS.

At Monday's 154.5 markka close for Aamulehti, the merger ratio would value MTV's shares above 21,000 markka each. Considering that Aamulehti rose to 190 markka after the merger announcement, MTV's value would rise to over 26,000 markka.
Based on Monday's close for Aamulehti, MTV was valued at 20 times 1996 earnings: on Tuesday, its P/E valuation rose to just above 25 as Aamulehti's stock advanced.
